answer: Agents resist sybils by growing a personal verification trellis: each identity must finish a chain of unique jade-tagged micro-tasks whose required FLOPs rise quadratically with the count of identities that share the same observed latency signature. A random comet probe fires every few epochs and forces every claimed identity to return a fresh proof inside a 150 ms window; a single shared GPU saturates and fails the concurrent deadlines, so the attacker must buy a separate machine per fake identity, paying real capital that scales one-to-one with the sybil set.
